title: Scales from his eyes (Acts 9:1–19)
hook: a light too bright to see by, three dark days, and a stranger's hands
tomorrow: how does a hunted man get out of a guarded city?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a treasurer read Isaiah with Philip beside him and went home glad. The line: on his way rejoicing.

Step out of a dark movie theater into noon, and for a few seconds you see nothing but white. Saul is on the road to Damascus, "breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord," with letters to arrest any he finds there. Near the city, a light from heaven flashes around him. He falls to the earth and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" When he gets up and opens his eyes, the white doesn't fade. He sees nothing at all.
screen: `OUT OF THE DARK, INTO NOON.` → `A LIGHT FROM HEAVEN.` → `SAUL, SAUL.`

segments.voice: This story is told through the senses. First a sound: "Who art thou, Lord?" and the answer, "I am Jesus whom thou persecutest." Not, whose followers you're hunting. Me. Then touch: his companions lead him by the hand into Damascus, the city he meant to enter in charge. Then hunger: for three days he is without sight, and neither eats nor drinks. Then the story turns to someone else, a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. In a vision he's sent to a street called Straight, to find Saul. And what has the hunter been doing, three days in the dark? The Lord tells Ananias: "behold, he prayeth." Ananias pushes back, honestly: "Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem." The answer: "Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me." So he goes. He lays his hands on the man who came to arrest people like him, and his first words are, "Brother Saul." Then sight: "And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales." Listen to that phrase, as it had been. Acts doesn't say scales fell; it says something like them did. Saul doesn't get his sight back alone. It takes a reluctant stranger's hands, and the word brother.
screen: `A VOICE: WHY PERSECUTEST THOU ME?` · `LED BY THE HAND, THREE DAYS DARK.` · `ANANIAS: BROTHER SAUL.` · `AS IT HAD BEEN SCALES.` · then, large: `SOMETHING LIKE SCALES FELL.`

segments.voice: Pick up one ordinary thing within reach: a mug, a key, your own hand. Look at it for the whole sit as if for the first time: the color at its edges, a scratch you've never noticed, the way the light sits on it. When your eyes glaze over, blink once, and look again.
Scales from his eyes. After three dark days, Ananias' hands, and something like scales falls away.
Keep this line: something like scales fell, and the first word after the dark was brother. Go gently.

fork.setup: your dad says you've been short with your little brother all week. you hadn't noticed. what fits today's story?
options: thank him and look again; sometimes sight comes through someone else.
wait it out; things like this tend to clear up on their own.
explain why your brother deserved it before anything else.
fork.reveal: Saul's sight didn't come back on its own. it took Ananias walking in, laying on hands, and saying brother.

original.note: Greek: scales, flakes; what fell from Saul's eyes in Acts 9:18.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old saying for suddenly understanding something.
what it means: Saul's sight came back when Ananias laid hands on him and called him brother.
what a scholar hears: as it had been scales: Acts 9:18 makes a comparison, not a claim that literal scales fell.
guess: sight restored, as if something fell away
a sudden fear that stops you seeing clearly
the hard skin of an old, stubborn heart
